name: Ertapenem
route_note: Once-daily IV infusion or IM injection; suited to outpatient parenteral therapy.

discovery.note: A 1-beta-methyl carbapenem with a benzoic-acid side chain that increases protein binding and prolongs half-life.

tagline: Once-daily carbapenem for ESBL infections, without anti-pseudomonal activity
summary: Ertapenem is a long-acting carbapenem given once daily. It covers ESBL-producing Enterobacterales, streptococci, methicillin-susceptible staphylococci and anaerobes, but not Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter or enterococci, which makes it a narrower carbapenem option.
mechanism: Ertapenem binds penicillin-binding proteins (notably PBP2 and PBP3 of E. coli) and inhibits cell-wall synthesis.

It is stable to ESBL and AmpC enzymes but not carbapenemases. High plasma protein binding gives a long half-life, while its negative charge reduces penetration through Pseudomonas porins, explaining the gap in spectrum.
uses: Complicated urinary tract infections including pyelonephritis
Prophylaxis of surgical site infection after colorectal surgery

history.title: First carbapenem
history.detail: Imipenem/cilastatin is approved in the US, establishing the carbapenem class.

history.title: Meropenem
history.detail: Meropenem, a DHP-I-stable carbapenem, is approved in the US.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Invanz, a once-daily carbapenem.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Ertapenem is authorised in the European Union.

history.title: NDM-1 described
history.detail: Description of the NDM-1 metallo-beta-lactamase highlights the spread of carbapenem resistance, prompting carbapenem-sparing stewardship.

pk.metabolism: hydrolysis of the beta-lactam ring to inactive metabolite

facts: Ertapenem's once-daily dosing makes it one of the few carbapenems commonly used for home IV therapy.
